assessments.reasoning: Lines 25–42 in the pinned TOP reference support ordered TOP as an ordered row limit. Lines 75–77 also name SET ROWCOUNT as an alternative row limiter. Microsoft's SET ROWCOUNT article at the identical commit confirms at lines 53–58 that a positive smaller ROWCOUNT overrides SELECT TOP at execution time. The frozen conditions leave the effective ROWCOUNT unrestricted even though the machine value states that TOP takes the first requested number of rows.

challenge.method: Checked the TOP introduction, the outer UNION versus same-subquery ordering example at lines 91–148, and the same-scope OFFSET/FETCH restriction at line 165. Acquired the sibling SET ROWCOUNT Markdown at commit a52ca41720ddecda8407b735a031a8559e75bf8c and checked its applicability monikers and Remarks. SHA-256 dc51015e6261063277ea74a2ca587b3310b319e670382b04d3130fd5d1deed26.
challenge.results: The same-scope ordering selects the ordered prefix in the ordinary case. With five qualifying rows and TOP (5) plus ORDER BY in one query scope, an active SET ROWCOUNT 2 can still cap the result at two rows. This documented configuration meets the frozen ordered-SELECT conditions and defeats an exact-N reading. https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MicrosoftDocs/sql-docs/a52ca41720ddecda8407b735a031a8559e75bf8c/docs/t-sql/statements/set-rowcount-transact-sql.md

limitations: An exact-N finding needs an effective ROWCOUNT of zero or at least N, in addition to a valid ordered query and sufficient rows. The pinned TOP passage remains evidence for a bounded ordered-limit description.
